task.description: Follow-up fix on Step 3: REQ-376's EO-003 (a process instance with history in an already-retired month still replays its complete step history with no gap and no error after retirement) required extending Letflow.EventStore.query_instance_events/3 (event_store.ex ~line 1256) to UNION events and events_archive and merge/sort results -- a deliberate, required behavior change per decision 0037 and design doc section 6. This newly exposed a stale assertion in a PRE-EXISTING REQ-025 test (test/letflow/event_store_test.exs, describe "read/2: not-found vs. legitimately-empty (AC2)", test named "an instance that had events, now fully archived, returns {:ok, []} -- NOT :instance_not_found") which encoded the OLD pre-REQ-376 behavior (read/2 only looked at the live events table). Update that ONE test to correctly document the NEW EO-003 behavior, grep for any other similarly-stale archived-event-invisible assumption, and verify.
acceptance_criteria: test/letflow/event_store_test.exs's fully-archived-instance test rewritten to expect the archived event back via read/2, not {:ok, []}
describe/test names and surrounding comments updated to reflect the new still-readable-when-fully-archived framing
sibling not-found test left untouched unless a real problem is found
grep for other archive( -> read assertions; fix any other stale one found, or state explicitly none exist
mix test test/letflow/event_store_test.exs run and confirmed passing, real output quoted
fix committed and pushed to feature/WF02-REQ376-20260922, handoff written

result.summary:
Read design doc section 6 (EO-003) to confirm exact semantics: retire_month/3 never deletes rows, only reparents a partition from events to events_archive; query_instance_events/3 now runs two queries (against Event and ArchivedEvent, both scoped by instance_id and apply_read_filter/2), concatenates and re-sorts by sequence_number. This applies to BOTH the new partition-retirement mechanism and the pre-existing row-level archive/1 move path (ArchivedEvent rows), since both land data in events_archive -- so archive/1 (REQ-025/REQ-026) is a valid, in-scope trigger for exercising this test, not a mismatched mechanism.

Rewrote test/letflow/event_store_test.exs's describe block 'read/2: not-found vs. legitimately-empty (AC2)' -> 'read/2: not-found vs. still-readable-when-fully-archived (AC2)', and its second test (previously 'an instance that had events, now fully archived, returns {:ok, []} -- NOT :instance_not_found') -> 'an instance that had events, now fully archived, still replays them via read/2 -- NOT :instance_not_found, NOT silently empty (EO-003)'. The test now captures the seeded event's event_id from seed_event!/6's return value, archives it, and asserts {:ok, [event]} = EventStore.read(...) with field-level assertions (event_id, instance_id, sequence_number, event_type) matching this test file's existing assertion-detail style elsewhere (e.g. the AC1 describe block). Updated the block's leading comment to explain the pre-REQ-376 vs post-REQ-376 framing and cite decision 0037 / design doc section 6. Left the sibling 'no instance_sequence row -> :instance_not_found' test untouched -- confirmed it exercises ensure_instance_started/2's STEP 1 existence check, an unrelated code path unaffected by the query_instance_events/3 union change.

Grepped test/letflow/event_store_test.exs (and the wider test/ tree) for 'events_archive', 'archive(', 'moved_count' near a read/2 assertion: found 6 other archive( call sites in this file (AC4 idempotency, AC6 retention-policy x3, INV-AR-2, event_payload_store FK-ordering test) -- none of them call read/2 (or point_in_time/3) after archiving; they only assert table_count/Repo.get_by against Event/ArchivedEvent directly. No other stale assertion of this kind exists in the test suite.

Verification: docker exec letflow-postgres-1 psql confirmed 0 active letflow_test connections before starting. `mix test test/letflow/event_store_test.exs` (real Postgres, letflow_test): Result: 28 passed, 0 failures, 0 warnings, in 65-78s (two runs) -- 28 is this file's full test count (confirmed via grep -c '  test '), all passing including the rewritten test. Attempted the full `mix letflow.check.test` gate (this task's own mandatory pre-handoff check) once: it failed with DBConnection.ConnectionError / Postgrex 'too many clients already' from scripts/test_parallel.sh's parallel partitions -- traced via `docker exec ... psql -c "SELECT count(*), application_name FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname LIKE 'letflow_test%' GROUP BY application_name"` to 40 live connections from two OTHER concurrent sessions (letflow_mixtest_53908_grptp1011063, letflow_mixtest_62308_grptp1011063), i.e. real cross-session DB contention, not a failure caused by this change -- exactly the scenario this dispatch's own instruction (item 6) anticipated and told me to fall back from. Did not force a retry against that contention (mix letflow.check.test has no file-scoped/bare-mix-test mode -- it always shells out to the full N-way scripts/test_parallel.sh); the scoped `mix test test/letflow/event_store_test.exs` run above is the verification evidence for this specific fix. This diff adds no new test helper with a default argument, so ISS-0069's dead-default-argument class (the specific thing mix letflow.check.test's substring check guards) does not apply to this change.

Note for the record: an earlier draft of this turn used Bash run_in_background + a cross-turn wait for mix letflow.check.test's first (contended) attempt, which a sibling session correctly flagged as the ISS-0213/ISS-0223 stalled-background-wait anti-pattern. Corrected within this same turn -- the actual verification and commit above were completed via direct, foreground, in-turn commands.
result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-gate on this fix (single-test change, EO-003 semantics confirmed against design doc section 6, 28/28 passing).
